description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: lib/File/Spec.pm `canonpath` (the shim, File::Spec::Unix::_pp_canonpath's six substitutions verbatim); catfile calls it on the file AND, through catdir, on the joined directory.  perl itself runs an XS canonpath; PCL runs six regex substitutions, each a do-regex-subst with its scanner (do-regex-subst 48 % of a catfile loop, sb-sprof).  File::Spec->catfile measured 5.0 us a call under PCL against 0.47 us in perl (shimbench, exploratory).

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/shim/m-canon-ab.pl: the shipped body vs the same body behind `return $path if index($path,'//') < 0 && index($path,'/.') < 0 && substr($path,0,2) ne './' && substr($path,-1) ne '/'`; 15 probe paths compared first, including '', '.', '/', './', '//', '/./', 'a/.b', 'x/..'; 200 k calls; legs/leg2.log): PCL 1.53 -> 0.47 us a call; perl 0.27 -> 0.24 us (the guard is also free in perl).

THE FIX: the guard in lib/File/Spec.pm canonpath (a plainer Perl body -- rule 9a: the shim is the layer).  Optionally the same idea in catdir's join.

BAR: the File::Spec / Path-Tiny board files one-file (`tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows Path-Tiny t/...`), the gate rows naming canonpath/catfile, the 15 probe paths as guard rows (perl's answers), everyday.

DO NOT: drop any of the six substitutions or reorder them; a path containing `/.` anywhere (also `/.hidden`) takes the full body -- the guard is deliberately conservative.
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): File::Spec's canonpath (behind every catfile / catdir -- 1,565 call sites over perl's lib + the board dists) runs SIX s/// on every path; a guard that returns an already-clean path unchanged is -69 % (1.53 -> 0.47 us a call under PCL)
